text_to_speech: Hello astronomers! When you want to do professional level astronomy, whether you are an amateur or researcher, the quality of the sky is very important. That’s why astronomical observatories are built at remote locations. Today, we’re in Val di Fiemme, one of the most beautiful locations of the Dolomites, and it is here we find the impressive astronomical observatory of the “Fiemme Astronomy Association“ From this impressive place, amateur astronomers actually conduct global outreach by showing the beauty of the night sky to those vacationing in nearby hotels, visiting from all around the world! To accomplish this, they have installed a large 20 inches diameter Ritchey-Chretien telescope, together with a 7 inches diameter apochromatic refractor in parallel. Everything mounted together on a large equatorial mount. The problem they face here is the same problem that astronomers face all over the world. How to remotely control and power all the devices they need to use with their telescope. For example, because of the dimensions of the entire instrument, if they have a computer in a separate control room they can’t connect a planetary USB camera because the USB 3 cable would simply be too long. The solution is the EAGLE. Computer, power distribution, dew control and more, all in a single, solid component that becomes a structural, integrated part of your telescope. This way they can connect all the cameras and other devices directly to the EAGLE, with short USB or power cables, and eliminate other needless complexity. Clumsy power supplies from all of their 12 volt devices like cooled cameras, focusers and rotators can be eliminated because they can now be powered directly through the EAGLE - they even be remotely powered on and off. They can connect to their EAGLE directly via its integrated WiFi networking or via a standard Ethernet cable to control the telescope. This can also allow the EAGLE to access the Internet for true remote access, and stream their images in real time to a large screen for the observatory visitors. All of these capabilities make the EAGLE the ultimate solution to remotely access your observatory - allowing you tighter integration and control of all the devices used in your astronomical observatory! For more content that will help you to explore the Universe like a pro, subscribe to our channel and clear skies!

youtube_description:
Astronomical observatories are often installed in remote and isolated places to avoid light pollution. In this video we discover how EAGLE helps control the remote observatory starting from the example of the Fiemme Astronomy Association that has an important astronomical observatory in Tesero (TN - Italy). The amateur astronomers in Fiemme Astronomy Association conduct global outreach by showing the beauty of the night sky to those vacationing in nearby hotels, visiting from all around the world! But the problem they face is how to remotely control and power all the devices installed in the telescopes, since the cables to connect to computer in control room are too long. Let's see how we solved the problem by installing EAGLE directly on the telescope.
Read the complete article in our website: https://www.primalucelab.com/astronomy/blog/remote-observatory-eagle-osservatorio-remoto/
